<dir>/tsconfig.json, silently dropping the parent's paths.

ix-cli: 940 passed, 1 skipped. typecheck, lint, knip clean.

perf(ingest): memoize module resolution

Resolution runs per bound relationship, and index.ts issues two full lookups
of the same (source, specifier, kind) triple for each one, so a repo with
paths/baseUrl pays the walk over and over.

Cache on the three things that actually change the answer: the source
directory (which config applies), the source extension (a .js caller prefers
.js over .ts), and the specifier and kind. Keying on the directory alone —
the obvious shortcut — would serve a .js caller's answer to a .ts caller in
the same folder and silently flip the preference order, so there is a test
that runs both orders and a repeat.

Measured on a synthetic 2000-file workspace, 1000 calls across 50 source
directories: 24.87us/call -> 3.38us/call, ~7.4x.

ix-cli: 941 passed, 1 skipped. typecheck, lint, knip clean.

fix(ingest): bound and confine tsconfig reads

Three holes on the config-reading path, all reachable from repo content
because tsconfig.json is repo content, and all reachable before ingestion's
own size gate — createTypeScriptModuleResolver is built at ingest.ts:1049,
51 lines ahead of the MAX_FILE_BYTES check.

1. No size cap. readObject read and parsed any tsconfig whole. A 64 MB JSONC
   file — which git packs down to a ~95 KB repo — gives
   FatalProcessOutOfMemory, signal 6, which the surrounding try/catch cannot
   catch. main skips that file as tooLarge, so this was the first pre-gate
   whole-file read and it bypassed an existing control.

2. Device nodes and FIFOs. openSync follows symlinks, so a link committed
   inside the repo pointing at /dev/zero read forever, and one pointing at a
   FIFO blocked the event loop. Both report size 0, so a size check alone
   does not help. Under MCP this is worse than a slow ingest: the in-process
   runner means withTimeout can never fire and the server wedges
   uncancellably.

3. No containment. resolveExtends only checked value.startsWith("."), which
   is not containment — nodePath.resolve clamps at the filesystem root, so
   enough .. segments name any absolute path from any depth. An ingested repo
   chose which files on the machine were read, and a config outside the
   workspace had its paths trusted.

Fixed by opening once and fstat-ing the same handle (no stat-then-read
window; the pattern ingest.ts already uses), rejecting anything that is not a
regular file or is over 1 MB, and filtering extends candidates to those
inside the workspace root.

No content ever escaped: resolveCandidate only consults an in-memory Map
built from the caller's file list, so an escaped read could not reach output.
This is availability plus unauthorized read, now closed.

3 tests, each mutation-tested. ix-cli: 944 passed, 1 skipped. typecheck,
lint, knip clean.

chore: use the \\x00 escape instead of a raw NUL byte

I used raw NUL separators in a lookup key. They are invisible in most editors
and diffs — they render as a space — so the CI guard is the only thing that
sees them, and it is there precisely because a raw NUL makes the file binary
to grep/ripgrep, which then silently skips it.

The escape is the same byte at runtime, so behaviour and tests are unchanged.

fix(ingest): open config files non-blocking, and don't half-load a dropped extends

Three fixes from a rescan of the previous security commit.

1. The FIFO guard could never fire. Opening a FIFO for reading blocks until a
   writer appears, so the isFile() check — which runs after the open — was
   never reached. My comment credited it with stopping "a FIFO (blocks the
   event loop forever)", a protection the code could not provide, and the
   passing /dev/zero test made that look verified: a character device opens
   fine, so it exercised a different path. A repo-committed symlink to any
   FIFO wedged `ix ingest` before the parsing phase even announces itself —
   no output, no timeout, no error. O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK makes the open
   return; the existing fstat/isFile guard then rejects it correctly.
   Undefined on Windows, where the bitwise-or degrades to a plain read and
   there is no FIFO to open this way.

2. Containment over-rejected a legitimate sibling. A bare startsWith("..")
   also matches a directory merely *named* with leading dots, so
   `..shared/tsconfig.json` inside the workspace read as an escape and was
   dropped silently. Compare path segments instead.

3. A dropped extends left a half-loaded config, which is worse than main. A
   scoped run (`ix map ./packages/web`) roots containment at the ingest path,
   so a monorepo's shared tsconfig.base.json one level up is correctly
   refused — but the remainder still carried the package's own `paths`,
   which then matched, failed against the missing baseUrl, and returned an
   *authoritative* empty. That suppresses the stem fallback and deletes an
   edge main resolves fine. Treat such a config as unusable, which is exactly
   main's behaviour.

knip.json: mkfifo added to ignoreBinaries for the new POSIX-gated test.

Each fix mutation-tested; removing O_NONBLOCK hangs the suite outright.
ix-cli: 947 passed, 1 skipped. typecheck, lint, knip and the NUL guard clean.

fix(ingest): check containment against the file actually opened

Containment was pure path arithmetic, which cannot see through a
symlinked directory: every segment of "./linked/tsconfig.json" is inside
the workspace even when `linked/` points elsewhere, so an ingested repo
could still choose a file outside the tree by shipping one link. The
lexical check stays — it is what stops `../` traversal from the config
text — and the resolved path is now checked as well.

The resolve happens while the handle is open and is confirmed to name the
same inode, so swapping the link between the open and the resolve cannot
smuggle an outside file in under an inside name.

The workspace root is resolved too. Comparing a resolved file against an
unresolved root rejects every config whenever the root is itself reached
through a link — macOS /var -> /private/var, a home on a network mount, a
~/code symlink — which would have switched tsconfig resolution off for
those users with no error. The matrix here is ubuntu + windows, so no
runner would have caught it; the added test uses a symlinked root.

comments.body:
Added one more commit (`adc97c1`) closing the symlink gap I flagged as non-blocking earlier.

Containment was pure path arithmetic, which cannot see through a symlinked directory: every segment of `./linked/tsconfig.json` is inside the workspace even when `linked/` points elsewhere, so an ingested repo could still name a file outside the tree by shipping one link. Wrote the failing test first to confirm the escape was real rather than theoretical.

The lexical check stays — it is what stops `../` traversal from the config text — and the resolved path is now checked too. The resolve happens while the handle is open and is confirmed to name the same inode, so swapping the link between the open and the resolve cannot smuggle an outside file in under an inside name.

The part I would most like a second pair of eyes on: **the workspace root is resolved too.** Comparing a resolved file against an unresolved root rejects every config whenever the root is itself reached through a link — macOS `/var` -> `/private/var`, a home on a network mount, a `~/code` symlink. That would have switched tsconfig resolution off entirely for those users, with no error and nothing in CI to catch it, since the matrix here is ubuntu + windows. The added test uses a symlinked root specifically to hold that down.

Both halves mutation-tested: dropping the containment call fails only the escape test, and comparing against the unresolved root fails only the symlinked-root test. Full `test:unit` is 949 passing.

Context for the review: this is the same module where my earlier "fix" for FIFOs shipped a guard that could not fire (the non-regular-file check sat *after* an open that blocks forever on a FIFO), with a comment asserting it worked and a passing `/dev/zero` test that exercised a different path. That is why I am flagging the root-resolution decision explicitly rather than letting it ride on my own reading.

Found and independently verified an additional ingest correctness regression in the current #445 implementation: a configured module mapping names the module authoritatively, but the renamed-import fallback still binds `import { Base as LocalBase } from "@core"` to a class method `W.Base` — a member can never be a module export — emitting a confident wrong EXTENDS edge (@0.9) where the base never had one. The same happens for `import { type User as ExternalUser }`, which emits REFERENCES to `W.User`.

The issue is still reproducible against the current upstream PR state (head `adc97c1`), and I did not find an existing fix or duplicate PR addressing it.

Follow-up commit `f9274cc` applies the minimal fix — the same plain-key requirement on the configured-binding path — and adds regression coverage for the configured renamed EXTENDS and REFERENCES cases.

Verification: resolveEdges 72/72 on the fix tree, `tsc` clean; the wrong edges reproduce against `adc97c1` and are eliminated after.

Follow-up commit:
https://github.com/Alot1z/Ix-remap/commit/f9274cc0870c65a496a5b983c814d9fed6a65c0f

This is ready for the PR author/maintainer to review/cherry-pick.

pull_requests.title: fix(ingest): resolve renamed type imports, with a default-import guard
pull_requests.body:
Carries **@Hiro-Chiba's #434** plus one review fix. Landing it here closes #434 as merged.

> ⚠️ **Merge with a merge commit, not squash.** This branch contains Hiro-Chiba's commit alongside mine; a squash would collapse an external contributor's work into one commit authored by me.

## Their change (`819d67e`)

Resolves renamed consumer-side TS bindings for inheritance and type references — `import { Base as LocalBase }` now resolves `EXTENDS`/`REFERENCES`/`CALLS` to the provider's real symbol.

## My fix (`eab1075`)

The fallback matched `binding.imported` against every parsed symbol in the provider file. For `import run from "./m"`, `binding.imported` is the literal sentinel `'default'` (set at `index.ts:514`), not an export name — and `fileHasSymbol` holds every entity including non-exported methods. So any provider member *called* `default` satisfied it:

```
/repo/m.ts  export class M { default() { return 1; } }
            export default new M();
/repo/n.ts  import run from "./m"; export function go() { return run(); }
```

main emits nothing; #434 emits `CALLS go -> m.ts` with `dstQualifiedKey: "M.default"` at **0.9** — confident, and wrong. Guarded with the same `!== 'default'` exclusion `index.ts:3199` already uses.

CI was green because every existing default-import test uses a *named* default export, which resolves before the fallback is reached.

## Verification

Mutation-tested: delete the guard and the added test alone goes red. `tsc --noEmit` clean; core-ingestion shows the same 6 pre-existing fixture-missing failures as the untouched base.

Reviewed as part of a full pass over all 9 open PRs; the per-PR findings and a security review of the combined tree are in the thread on #434.

pull_requests.title: fix(php): resolve imports by namespace, with clause-scoping and DoS fixes
pull_requests.body:
Carries **@Hiro-Chiba's #442** plus three review fixes, one a DoS. Landing it here closes #442 as merged.

> ⚠️ **Merge with a merge commit, not squash** — contains Hiro-Chiba's two commits alongside mine.

## Their change (`ea79b11`, `83079ff`)

Resolves explicit PHP type imports by declared namespace instead of a repo-wide short-name match. The follow-up replaces the flagged ReDoS regex with a char-code trim — **the CodeQL alert on #442 is stale** and can be dismissed after a re-scan.

## My fixes

**1. `5c322a9` — the capture also matched the alias.** Confirmed against the grammar by dumping the parse tree: in `namespace_use_clause` the alias is a **direct `(name)` sibling** of the `qualified_name`, so `[(qualified_name) (name)]` captured both. `use Vendor\Package\User as Admin;` emitted an `IMPORTS` edge to an unrelated `Admin` class and promoted the wrong short-name matches from 0.5 to **0.9** — the opposite of this PR's purpose. Anchored to the clause's first named child; bare `use GlobalThing;` is a lone `(name)` child and still matches.

Two related bugs shared that root cause: `importAliased` was computed from the whole statement, so one alias in a comma-separated `use` disabled FQCN resolution for every clause; and that same unanchored `/\s+as\s+/` was a second ReDoS instance CodeQL missed (~3.7 s on a `use` padded with 100k spaces, which is valid PHP). Reading the clause node removes both.

**2. `663c6ce` — two regressions measured against main, not inferred.**
- A `use` leaked across braced namespace blocks: `go()` in `namespace B` resolved to the vendor file at 0.9 although `B` declares its own `Thing` two lines up. main emits no edge at all.
- Duplicate `CALLS` edges reached the graph: `phpCallKind` splits the dedup key, so `log()` and `Logger::log()` survive as two relationships; when both resolve to the same member, patch-builder salted the edge id by call kind and emitted two `UpsertEdge` ops with identical src/dst/predicate but different ids — and the dedup downstream keys on id. Measured main 1 op, this branch 2.

**3. `7c8a387` — one ordinary PHP file hung ingestion (the DoS).** `phpNamespaceForNode` rescanned the file's top-level nodes for every definition. A valid PSR-12 file — `namespace App\Support` plus ~16k functions, 890 KB, under the 1 MB cap — took **over three minutes**. `.php` is ingested by default, the minified-file skip needs a ≥20k-char line, and `ParsePool` has no per-file timeout, so one file pins a worker; PHP is also in `PARSER_DERIVED_PRESCAN`, so it's parsed twice.

| declarations | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 2,000 | 3,245 ms | 104 ms |
| 4,000 | 13,099 ms | 151 ms |
| 8,000 | 54,408 ms | 236 ms |

Entity counts and `packageScope` values identical at every size.

Worth flagging, since it wasn't what I first assumed: mutation testing showed the binary search is *not* load-bearing, and even rebuilding the span list per definition stays fast. The dominant cost is `namedChild(i)` materializing a node wrapper per index — iterating `namedChildren` once is the real fix. The regression test times out only against the exact original.

## Known gap, not fixed here

My multi-namespace guard counts distinct `packageScope` strings, so it misses two blocks sharing a name and a `use`-only block. Cheap follow-up: count the `module` entities the parse already emits per braced block.

## Verification

Every fix mutation-tested. core-ingestion 338 passed, 6 pre-existing failures unchanged from base; `tsc --noEmit` clean.

commits.message: fix(php): resolve imports by namespace
fix(php): bound namespace trimming

fix(php): scope use-clause parsing to the clause, not the statement

Two defects, one root cause: both the query and the alias flag looked at the
whole 'use' declaration instead of the individual clause.

1. Phantom imports. In 'use Vendor\\Package\\User as Admin' the alias is a
   direct (name) sibling of the (qualified_name), so the unanchored
   alternation captured it as a second imported module. Ix then matched
   'Admin' against an unrelated class of that name, emitting an IMPORTS edge
   the file never declares and promoting the wrong short-name matches from
   0.5 to 0.9 — the exact class of error this PR exists to remove. Anchoring
   the capture to the clause's first named child fixes it; a bare
   'use GlobalThing;' is a lone (name) child and still matches.

2. Comma-separated imports. importAliased came from a regex over the whole
   statement, so 'use A\\One\\Alpha, A\\Two\\Beta as Bee;' flagged every clause
   as aliased and silently disabled FQCN resolution for Alpha. Reading the
   clause node instead scopes it correctly.

Deriving the flag from the node also deletes an unanchored /\\s+as\\s+/ over
repo-controlled text — the same polynomial-backtracking class CodeQL flagged
at phpTypeFqcn, in a spot it did not flag. Measured at ~3.7s on a use
statement padded with 100k spaces, which parses as valid PHP.

The two anchored kind regexes (^use function, ^use const) are linear and
unchanged.

core-ingestion: 334 passed, 6 pre-existing failures unchanged from base.

fix(php): scope use to its namespace block, and stop double-emitting calls

Two further regressions against main, both measured rather than inferred.

1. A use leaked across braced namespace blocks. phpFqcnImportsByLocal is
   keyed by file, but a use is scoped to its namespace block. Given

     namespace A { use Vendor\\Package\\Thing; function run(Thing $t) {...} }
     namespace B { class Thing {} function go(Thing $t) {...} }

   go() resolved to Vendor/Package/Thing.php at 0.9, though B declares its
   own Thing right there. main emits no edge for go at all. One namespace per
   file is the PSR-12 norm, so the index now skips a multi-block file rather
   than mis-resolve it, restoring main's behaviour exactly for that shape.

2. Duplicate CALLS edges reached the graph. phpCallKind splits the per-file
   dedup key, so log() and Logger::log() survive as two relationships. When
   both resolve to the same member, patch-builder salted the edge id by call
   kind and emitted two UpsertEdge ops with identical src, dst and predicate
   but different ids — and the dedup downstream keys on id, so both commit.
   Measured: main 1 op, this branch 2. The salt still applies when the two
   kinds resolve to different nodes, which is what it is for.

Both mutation-tested: each guard removed reds exactly its own test.
core-ingestion: 336 passed, 6 pre-existing failures unchanged from base.

fix(php): resolve a definition's namespace without rescanning the file

phpNamespaceForNode walked rootNode.namedChild(0..i) for every definition, so
one file cost O(definitions x top-level nodes). An ordinary, valid PSR-12 file
— namespace App\Support plus ~16k functions, 890 KB, comfortably under the
1 MB ingest cap — took over three minutes to parse, and nothing stops it:
.php is ingested by default, the minified-file skip needs a >=20k-char line,
and ParsePool has no per-file timeout, so one file pins a worker. PHP is also
in PARSER_DERIVED_PRESCAN, so the file is parsed twice.

Collect the unbraced namespace boundaries once per parse, mirroring how
goPackage is already hoisted, and binary-search them per definition. Braced
namespaces scope by containment and keep using the ancestor walk.

Measured on this machine, same file, entity counts and packageScope values
identical at every size:

  declarations   before      after
     2,000       3,245 ms    104 ms
     4,000      13,099 ms    151 ms
     8,000      54,408 ms    236 ms

Worth recording what mutation testing showed, since it is not what I first
assumed: swapping the binary search back for a linear scan over the spans
changes nothing, and even rebuilding the span list per definition stays fast.
The dominant cost is namedChild(i), which materializes a node wrapper per
index; iterating namedChildren once is what actually fixes it. The regression
test times out only against the exact original.

core-ingestion: 338 passed, 6 pre-existing failures unchanged from base.

chore: use the \\x00 escape instead of a raw NUL byte

I used raw NUL separators in a lookup key. They are invisible in most editors
and diffs — they render as a space — so the CI guard is the only thing that
sees them, and it is there precisely because a raw NUL makes the file binary
to grep/ripgrep, which then silently skips it.

The escape is the same byte at runtime, so behaviour and tests are unchanged.

fix(php): don't emit duplicate claims for a two-kind call

Same root cause as the duplicate edge fixed earlier in this branch, on the
claim path this time, and it fires on ordinary untyped PHP rather than an
exotic shape: phpCallKind splits the relationship dedup key, so
`handle(); $obj->handle();` survives as two relationships. A claim carries no
kind, so the two ops are byte-identical and nothing downstream can tell them
apart. Applied to both buildPatch and buildPatchWithResolution.

Contained today — stripMapModeOps drops all claims, so `ix map` never carried
these, and the only other consumer is a counter — but it inflates the counter
and would double-assert on any path that keeps claims.

Also tightens the namespace-scoping perf test from a 10s to a 3s timeout: the
fixed code runs in ~3ms and the old algorithm took ~12s, so 10s left only a
1.2x margin over the thing it is meant to catch.

Mutation-tested. core-ingestion: 339 passed, 6 pre-existing failures unchanged.

fix(php): count namespace blocks at the parser, not from entity scopes

The multi-namespace guard skipped a file when its entities carried more
than one distinct packageScope. Two shapes slip past that:

  namespace A { use Vendor\Thing; }   // declares nothing -> no scope
  namespace B { class Thing {} ... }

  namespace A { use Vendor\Thing; }   // two blocks, one scope *string*
  namespace A { class Thing {} ... }

In both, `use` from the first block was applied to the second, resolving
a name the second block declares itself and pointing it confidently at
the wrong file — the exact mis-resolution the guard exists to prevent.

Count `namespace_definition` nodes instead, which is what the guard
actually means. The count rides along on the walk that already collects
the unbraced spans: reading `namedChildren` a second time would pay the
node-wrapper materialization cost twice, and that term is what made the
original per-definition scan expensive.

`phpNamespaceBlocks` is spread in rather than assigned `undefined` so the
key is absent on non-PHP results — a present-but-undefined key still
serializes and would have rewritten every checked-in parseFile snapshot.

comments.body:
Added one more commit (`83b9be4`) after re-auditing the multi-namespace guard I wrote earlier in this PR. The guard was wrong in two reproducible ways.

It skipped a file when its entities carried more than one distinct `packageScope`. Two shapes slip past that:

```php
namespace A { use Vendor\Thing; }   // declares nothing -> contributes no scope
namespace B { class Thing {} ... }

namespace A { use Vendor\Thing; }   // two blocks, one scope *string*
namespace A { class Thing {} ... }
```

In both, the `use` from the first block was applied to the second — resolving a name the second block declares itself and pointing it confidently at the wrong file, which is precisely what the guard exists to prevent. Confirmed against real parser output before changing anything; the entity side genuinely cannot distinguish these.

It now counts `namespace_definition` nodes at the parser, which is what the guard actually means. The count rides along on the walk that already collects the unbraced spans — reading `namedChildren` a second time would pay the node-wrapper materialization cost twice, and that term is what made the original per-definition scan expensive.

Two tests cover the shapes above and a third asserts the common single-namespace file is still indexed, so "skip the ambiguous file" cannot quietly become "skip every file". All three go red against the old guard; the other 80 in the file stay green.

One near-miss worth recording: `phpNamespaceBlocks` is spread in rather than assigned `undefined`, because a present-but-undefined key still serializes and would have rewritten every checked-in `parseFile` snapshot — including TypeScript ones. That was invisible locally, since `doctor.ts`'s snapshot already fails on `main` for an unrelated reason and the failure *count* was unchanged. Verified the received parse result for `doctor.ts` is now byte-identical to `main`.

I reviewed the changes in #446 and independently reproduced the two multi-namespace cases the guard needs to handle:

- **Two braced blocks sharing one namespace name.** The entity-side guard added in `663c6ce` saw one distinct `packageScope` string (`size === 1`) and let the file through — applying one block's `use` to the other.
- **A `use`-only braced block.** It declares no type definitions, so it contributes no `packageScope` entry at all, yet its imports are still confined to it.

I validated a fork implementation against these cases: `0701040` (branch `fix/446-multi-namespace-guard`) counts namespace-definition module entities — excluding import-use modules via their IMPORTS relationships — instead of distinct scope strings, with two regression tests. The `resolveEdges` suite passes **82/82** against it.

The entity-count approach works, but it reconstructs the count from generated entities: it assumes every braced block (including use-only ones) emits a `kind:'module'` entity and that import-use modules stay identifiable. `83b9be4` removes that coupling — `phpNamespaceBlocks` counts the tree-sitter `namespace_definition` nodes directly, on the same single walk that already collects the unbraced spans (from `7c8a387`), so it cannot drift if entity emission changes and costs nothing extra. The same suite passes **83/83** against `83b9be4`.

For context, the guard's evolution is worth noting: `663c6ce` introduced the entity-side version; `7c8a387` replaced per-definition top-level scans with one precomputed walk + binary search (~197s → ~355ms on a ~16k-function PSR-12 file); `b07bff36` replaced a raw NUL byte with the `\x00` escape; `e786f20` deduplicates byte-identical claims for two-kind calls; `83b9be4` lands the parser-level count as the final form.

The fork branch is offered only as independent validation of the two shapes — not as a competing fix.

Quick clarification on the earlier fork references: the historical commits [`13b7bf0`](https://github.com/Alot1z/Ix-remap/commit/13b7bf0cc24cce7680ca5869be9f395894b03ff8), [`82aeb28`](https://github.com/Alot1z/Ix-remap/commit/82aeb285c3bc3ab516d0a7d1899ffee95bb52a40), and [`ece8195`](https://github.com/Alot1z/Ix-remap/commit/ece8195d71c439a69e79098ec8e3befe915532b7) were fork-side audit/communication artifacts and are not part of the #446 implementation. The current #446 implementation and regression coverage are contained in the upstream PR itself; the separate [`6a50e6c`](https://github.com/Alot1z/Ix-remap/commit/6a50e6cb2ab0790f0c594962f89e59ca6464dd70) fork commit is only an independent validation artifact. No changes to the #446 implementation are required from that validation.

Found one remaining PHP namespace-scope regression while adversarially re-auditing #446: `phpNamespaceBlocks` counts namespace-definition blocks but does not represent the global↔namespace boundary, so mixed-scope files could let the per-file FQCN import map cross that boundary and emit an incorrect high-confidence `CALLS` edge.

`0a7d97f` adds the minimal parser-level guard and regression coverage for the affected braced, unbraced, decoy, and reverse-direction cases. The relevant resolveEdges/query/patch-builder tests pass 113/113, with the regression reproduced against `83b9be4` before the fix and eliminated afterward.

Commit: https://github.com/Alot1z/Ix-remap/commit/0a7d97f6213e567bcd074ebe7fb41cd32b77e7c3

Found and independently verified one more PHP resolution regression in the current #446 implementation: `phpTypeFqcn` drops any entity carrying a `container`, and `findEnclosing`'s inclusive line ranges falsely nest two same-line sibling declarations — so `<?php namespace Vendor\Package; class A {} class B {}` plus `use Vendor\Package\B; new B()` resolves to nothing (NONE) both in-batch and through the global index, where base `043bc68` emitted IMPORTS @0.9.

The issue is still reproducible against the current upstream PR state (head `83b9be4`), and I did not find an existing fix or duplicate PR addressing it.

Follow-up commit `f577492` applies the minimal fix — drop the `entity.container` exclusion in `phpTypeFqcn`/`ambiguousPhpTypeNames`; PHP types (class/interface/trait/enum) can never be members, so a container on one is always a same-line artifact — and adds regression coverage for the same-line positive and multi-line control, in-batch and cross-batch.

Verification: resolveEdges/queries.php/patchBuilder.resolution 115/115, `tsc` clean; the regression reproduces against `83b9be4` and is eliminated after.

pull_requests.title: fix(ingest): confine discovered files to the directory being ingested
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

An ingested repository could name files outside itself and have them read into the graph.

`git ls-files` reports a committed symlink as an ordinary entry, and the `statSync` behind it describes the **target**. So a repo shipping

```
src/notes.ts -> ~/.ssh/id_rsa
```

had that file discovered, read, parsed, stored, and sent to the configured endpoint. `ix ingest --github owner/repo` runs this over repositories nobody has read, which makes repository contents attacker input — the same threat model that motivated the tsconfig hardening in #445.

`walkFiles` was never the hole: readdir Dirents describe the link itself, so `isFile()` is false for a symlink and it is skipped there. Git's list is the gap, and it is the path taken for anything that is a repository — so the safe-looking walker was never the one running.

## Type

- [x] Bug fix (security)

## Changes

- `discoverIngestFilePaths(discovered, root)` — canonicalize, de-duplicate, and confine to the directory actually asked for. Kept as one function rather than a filter at the call site so the confinement cannot be dropped without a test noticing.
- `isWithinDiscoveryRoot(root, candidate)` — segment-wise containment, so a sibling named `..shared/` is out but a child named `..shared/` is in.
- Dropped files are **counted and reported** (`skipped outside root` in the summary, `skipReasons.outsideRoot` in JSON) rather than silently vanishing.
- `tryGitLsFiles` exported for the test — the guarantee is a property of listing → canonicalize → confine *composed*, and each step looks fine alone.

## What deliberately still works

- **A symlink inside the tree.** Monorepos link packages around; confinement must not become "no symlinks at all". Held down by its own test.
- **An explicitly named single file.** Naming it IS the request, so there is nothing to escape from and no root is applied.

## Two things worth a reviewer's attention

**The root is canonicalized too.** Comparing a resolved file against an unresolved root drops *every* file whenever the root is itself reached through a link — macOS `/var` → `/private/var`, a home on a network mount, a `~/code` symlink. That reads as "this repo has no source files", with no error. The matrix here is ubuntu + windows, so no runner would ever catch it; the test builds a symlinked root deliberately.

**The escape test asserts the escape first.** It checks the outside path actually reaches discovery *before* checking that confinement drops it — otherwise it would pass just as well by discovering nothing at all.

## Validation

- Escape reproduced end-to-end against a real git repo with a committed symlink, then confirmed dropped.
- Mutation-tested, each killing exactly one test: dropping the filter, comparing against the unresolved root, and confining an explicitly named file.
- `npm run test:unit` — 68 files, 960 passed, 1 skipped. `typecheck`, `lint`, `knip` clean; no NUL bytes.
- Zero tracked symlinks across the local Ix / Ix-memory checkouts, so no behavioural change for ordinary repos.

comments.body:
Reviewed. The `paths` resolution and the `$`-token fix in `bf7a4b4` are both right, and the CodeQL alert on this PR is **stale** — its multi-star rationale is unreachable because `matchPathPattern` rejects a second `*` before substitution. Worth re-running the scan and dismissing.

Blocking issue: `return config?.baseUrl ? [] : undefined` makes a bare `baseUrl` authoritative. `[]` means *definitively not local*, and `baseUrl` matches every non-relative specifier — so on any repo that sets it (Next.js, CRA, Nest, most monorepo templates) every third-party import including `react` becomes an authoritative miss and its edges are dropped. Ix's own tsconfigs set neither `baseUrl` nor `paths`, so dogfooding can't see it.

Also flagging `resolveExtends`'s `existsSync`-then-read — CodeQL `js/file-system-race`, which this repo has a settled pattern for.

Both fixed, with 5 tests: **Hiro-Chiba/Ix#2**. Note it replaces your `treats an unresolved baseUrl module as authoritative` test — that behaviour is the defect. Your explicit-`paths` authority test is untouched and still passes.

Added a second commit to **Hiro-Chiba/Ix#2**: memoize the resolver.

Resolution runs per bound relationship and `index.ts` issues two full lookups of the same triple for each, so a repo with `paths`/`baseUrl` pays the walk repeatedly. Measured on a synthetic 2000-file workspace: **24.87 µs/call → 3.38 µs/call, ~7.4x**.

Worth flagging the trap, since the obvious key is wrong: `resolveCandidate` reads the source *extension* as well as the directory (a `.js` caller prefers `.js` over `.ts`). Keying on `dirname` alone serves one caller's answer to the other in the same folder and silently flips the preference order — there's a test that runs both orders plus a repeat, and it reds if the extension is dropped from the key.

comments.body:
Reviewed. The FQCN indexing is a real improvement and the `trimPhpNamespace` rewrite in `83079ff` correctly kills the flagged ReDoS — that CodeQL alert is **stale** and can be dismissed after a re-scan.

Blocking issue: widening the capture to `[(qualified_name) (name)]` also captures the alias, because in `namespace_use_clause` the alias is a direct `(name)` sibling. `use Vendor\\Package\\User as Admin;` therefore emits an `IMPORTS` edge to an unrelated `Admin` class the file never imports, and promotes the wrong short-name matches from 0.5 to **0.9** — the opposite of what this PR is for.

Two related clause-scoping bugs: `importAliased` is computed from the whole statement, so one alias in a comma-separated `use` disables FQCN resolution for every clause; and that same unanchored `/\\s+as\\s+/` is a second instance of the ReDoS class CodeQL missed (~3.7s on a `use` padded with 100k spaces, which is valid PHP).

All three fixed by one root-cause change — scope to the clause: **Hiro-Chiba/Ix#3**.

Added a second commit to **Hiro-Chiba/Ix#3** covering two further regressions I measured against main rather than inferred:

**1. A `use` leaks across braced namespace blocks.** `phpFqcnImportsByLocal` is keyed by file, but a `use` is scoped to its namespace block:

```php
namespace A { use Vendor\\Package\\Thing; function run(Thing $t) {...} }
namespace B { class Thing {} function go(Thing $t) {...} }
```

`go()` resolved to `Vendor/Package/Thing.php` at 0.9 although `B` declares its own `Thing` two lines up. main emits no edge for `go` at all. One namespace per file is the PSR-12 norm, so the index now skips a multi-block file rather than mis-resolve it — restoring main's behaviour exactly for that shape.

**2. Duplicate CALLS edges reach the graph.** `phpCallKind` splits the per-file dedup key, so `log()` and `Logger::log()` survive as two relationships. When both resolve to the same member, patch-builder salts the edge id by call kind and emits two `UpsertEdge` ops with identical `src`/`dst`/`predicate` but different ids — and the dedup downstream keys on id, so both commit. Measured: main 1 op, this branch 2. The salt still applies when the two kinds resolve to *different* nodes, which is what it's for.

pull_requests.title: fix(mcp): cap thrown error output, and keep the reason when the cap already fired
pull_requests.body:
Carries **@Hiro-Chiba's #426 and #436** plus one review fix. Landing it here closes both as merged.

> ⚠️ **Merge with a merge commit, not squash** — this branch contains two of Hiro-Chiba's commits alongside mine.

## Their changes

- `5e2bdcf` (#426) — a run whose captured output blew the byte cap now reports `ok: false`, so the MCP layer returns an `isError` result instead of a successful empty `structuredContent`. Verified this removes a divergence rather than creating one: the subprocess path already behaved this way via `maxBuffer`.
- `033181f` (#436) — routes thrown error text through the bounded-output collector so a crash can't blow the cap.

## My fix (`1f49d9f`)

`appendChunk` starts with `if (run.truncated) return;`, so routing thrown text through it means the text is **dropped outright** once the cap has fired. A command that floods and *then* throws reaches the client as:

```json
{"error": "[ix mcp] output exceeded N bytes and was truncated"}
```

for what was actually a crash. Before #436, `stderr: run.stderr.join("") + (failure ?? "")` appended it unconditionally — so this is a regression against main, in the one case where an operator most needs the reason. Keeps a bounded 2 KiB copy.

The normal path is untouched: a throw with no prior output still goes through `appendChunk` and is capped, which their existing test pins (verified unchanged — `run.truncated` is still false at that point).

## Verification

Mutation-tested: collapse the branch back to a bare `appendChunk` call and the new test goes red. ix-cli 932 passed, 1 skipped; `typecheck` and `knip` clean.

The security pass over the combined tree cleared this area specifically: truncation-to-error is strictly safer (it can only flip `ok` true→false, never mask a failure as success), and the failure detail is a single capped `stderr.push` in one `finally`, not repeatable within a run.
